quick_skim.title: UA-Bench: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models on Underwater Acoustic Recognition
quick_skim.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are fast becoming a general interface to sound, yet how far their broad pretraining carries into specialized domains remains largely open. Vessel monitoring, maritime safety, and ocean sensing all depend on recognizing underwater signals, but to our knowledge LALMs have not been systematically evaluated on them. Annotated recordings are costly to collect, and a faithful synthetic alternative has to bring together many interacting factors: the structure of detection pulses, communication waveforms, and ship-radiated noise, and the sound-speed profile, geometry, and multipath propagation through which each reaches the receiver. We address this by proposing \textbf{UA-Bench}, to our knowledge the first large-scale benchmark for evaluating LALMs on underwater acoustic signal recognition. It comprises 375,051 audio records that couple parameterized sources with modeled propagation, so that every record can be traced to the conditions that produced it. The records span these three signal families, and each carries a three-level label hierarchy (13 leaf classes), a templated multi-turn dialogue, and source and channel metadata. We evaluate on a balanced 2,600-record subset with a gated coarse-to-fine protocol that locates each error at source routing, fine-grained classification, or output format, and add a paired silent-audio control to test whether the waveform is actually used. Nine open LALMs, evaluated without task-specific adaptation, reach only 2.0\%--13.1\% leaf accuracy, against a random reference of 7.7\%. The waveform helps source routing far more than leaf recognition (for one model, +29.5 versus +2.3 points over silence), and just four models gain reliably at the leaf level, by at most 4.7 points. UA-Bench thus gives a reference point for these models, and its released training partition supports follow-up adaptation work.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Large audio-language models are untested on underwater acoustics; UA-Bench synthesizes detection pulses, communication waveforms and ship-radiated noise with realistic propagation to evaluate LALMs, revealing limited domain transfer and enabling standardized underwater target recognition benchmarking.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 大型音频语言模型已成为通用声音接口，但其在水下声学识别中的泛化能力仍不明确，而舰船辐射噪声等水下信号对海洋监测至关重要。作者提出首个水下声学识别基准UA-Bench，合成融合探测脉冲、通信波形与舰船辐射噪声并考虑声速剖面与多径传播的标注数据。系统评测显示现有大型音频语言模型在该任务上表现有限，暴露出明显的跨域泛化差距。该基准为水下目标识别提供了标准化评测平台，推动音频语言模型向海洋声学迁移。
